note: Two lists, and they say opposite things about their files.
`entries` is known FALSE POSITIVES of tools/release_screen.py's content sniffer.
An entry says: this file trips the sniffer, for this reason, and the reason is
not note text. Nothing here weakens the path rules — a file must already be
publishable by path to be sniffed at all.
`acknowledged` is the opposite claim: the hit is REAL, it is recorded, and it is
not fixed. It exists because a false-positive list is the wrong shape for a true
positive, and the alternatives are worse — deleting the file destroys an arm's
committed artefact to quiet a checker, and filing it under `entries` writes
'known false positive' next to something that is not one, in the exact place a
reader would go to check. Two extra fields are mandatory: `why_real` says why the
hit is genuine, `fixed_when` says what will clear it. An acknowledged violation
with no stated exit is a permanent exemption wearing a temporary label.
Neither list gates the exit code; `acknowledged` is printed in full on every run
instead, because it is a debt line rather than a status line. The gate that holds
it is this diff. Path rules are identical for both lists — an acknowledged entry
can no more name a corpus or sealed path than a false-positive one, and its
`sniff` is pinned the same way, so a DIFFERENT hit on an acknowledged file is
still UNEXPECTED and still fails. A path may appear in only one list.
`why_real` and `fixed_when` are committed prose and carry no surface form, span or
offset — the same rule as every other file here. Describing the shape of a
violation does not require quoting it.
Rules the screener enforces on this file, so they cannot be quietly relaxed:
- Literal paths only. No wildcards, no directory prefixes. The lesson of the
data/acquire/*.sh bypass is that a whitelist keyed on anything broader than
a filename stops naming what it permits.
- Nothing under data/ or sealed/, and nothing the deny rules cover. Those are
corpus and sealed paths; a sniffer hit on one of them is the alarm, not a
nuisance. data/README.md is excluded too, even though it is publishable: it
is the one file published out of a denied prefix, so it is the last file
that should be exemptible from the content check as well.
- `sniff` pins WHICH kind of hit is expected. A file allowlisted for Korean
prose that starts tripping the clinical-header pattern is reported as
unexpected, because that is a different fact about the file.
- `why` has to be a real sentence. An entry nobody can evaluate later is an
entry that gets renewed forever.
Reasons are written in English deliberately: Korean prose in this file would
trip HANGUL_PROSE and the allowlist would need an entry for itself.

entries.why: Project instructions, written in Korean. Prose about the rules — including the rule against putting corpus text in files like this one. No corpus text.
Korean comments explaining the corpora: and sealed: keys. This is the committed template and holds no real path; the machine's real paths live in data_paths.local.yaml, which is gitignored.

Korean comments explaining the document-type cue file: why the derivation is config rather than code, why the version field is written into every metrics.json, and how these patterns differ from the pre-seal measurement they were rewritten from. The values are German clinical vocabulary used as regexes (imaging modalities, specimen and ward words) in the same category as a rule file's patterns — general register terms, no document id, no span, no offset, no PHI surface form, and nothing read out of sealed/.
Korean comments documenting the identifier vocabulary. The values are experiment identifiers; the prose explains what each axis is for.
Korean comments explaining the error-sample parameters and why changing them invalidates a port-human run. Holds four integers and two strings; no span, no offset, no corpus text.

Korean comments explaining the constructed-split parameters for the corpora that ship no official split, and why editing an entry after a split is frozen re-opens the seal. Holds three proportions, a stratification variable, a stratum count and a seed; no document id, no span, no offset, no corpus text.

Korean prose recording the first port-oneshot run on es-meddocan: that it was a format failure, the validator's own error message, the cost and model-id fields, and the lifecycle record. No corpus text and no rule content beyond counts by layer — the failure was a markdown fence at line 1, so the position is quoted and the offending line is not, which is the same rule the validator message follows.

Korean write-up of the de-grascco port-oneshot run: cost, leak rate, complementarity, the per-type and per-document-type breakdowns, and the one rule that produced 144 of the 226 false positives. Counts, rates and rule_ids only — the rule_ids are already in the committed rule file, and no span, offset or note surface appears.

Korean prose recording the port-oneshot-nofence run on es-meddocan: the frozen window, the scoring (leak rate in both modes, P/R/F1, the complementarity decomposition and per-type leak), the cost and model-id fields, and the lifecycle record. Rule content is rule_id, layer and phi_type only — no pattern, no cue word, no term list — so nothing here reproduces what the rules match, and no corpus text, span or offset appears. The per-type tables are counts against gold, which is what results/**/metrics.json already publishes by path.

Korean prose recording the first port-multi run on es-meddocan: that the Profiler step was a format failure, the validator's own message, what is and is not on disk, the cost and model-id fields, the lifecycle record, and the finding that this is the second fence failure in the repository. No corpus text, span or offset appears. The response is not quoted — only its line count, the position the parser stopped at, and that the fence encloses every non-empty line, which is the same rule the validator message follows. The diagnostic section reports the validated profile as field values from closed naming.yaml vocabularies plus the count of type labels and of resolved cites; the one label list it names is the eight XML coarse categories, which DESIGN 9.0 already publishes.

Korean prose recording the completed port-loop arm on es-meddocan: the frozen window, the eight-round trajectory with each round's step-or-decay verdict, the final round's scoring in both modes with the complementarity decomposition and per-type leak, the cost split into published and abandoned spend, the defect list, and the §4 comparison against the baseline. It quotes no rule content at all — not even a rule_id, since the arm's rule_id findings are argued in the acknowledged entries below by mechanism rather than by token — and no corpus text, span or offset appears. Every table is counts and rates against gold, which results/**/metrics.json already publishes by path, plus token and wall figures from the cost blocks and the call log.

Korean prose reviewing which Bedrock model families could run the port-oneshot baseline after port-human's retirement (DESIGN 4.1). Holds model ids, a probe result table, and the trade-offs of each option. No corpus text, no spans: the only strings sent to Bedrock to produce it were 'Reply with the single word: ok'.

The Korean is the note this tool writes: render() composes docs/notes/call-variance.md's headings, its per-draw tables and the sentence warning that a rule_id Jaccard is not a behavioural figure. Same false positive as tools/release_screen.py's, one sniffer over — a tool whose output is Korean prose holds Korean prose as literals. It sends a committed prompt template and a corpus id and holds no span, offset, matcher or document text; its draws are loaded out of a temporary directory and its rows carry counts, rule_ids and hashes only.

Korean prose recording how far the same prompt's output moves when the input does not: rule counts, rule_id overlap, layer distributions, completion tokens and response hashes across repeated calls. rule_id values are agent-authored identifiers this screener already checks against a vocabulary, and no matcher, span, offset or document text is recorded. The Korean here is the note's own explanation of why the probe does not score dev.

Korean prose recording whether a prompt with its example removed still returns an artefact its own validator accepts: outcome, rule and flag counts, layer and phi_type histograms, refusal reason names, token counts, wall seconds, and prompt and response hashes. Same shape as docs/notes/call-variance.md's entry, one probe over. The Korean is the note's explanation of what n=1 does and does not establish against the measured pass records it is traded for. No span, offset, matcher or document text: the probe invents the three lines it sends, and the auditor rows record refusal reason names and per-type counts rather than the positions they were refused at.

Korean prose recording that a practice session happened before port-human iteration 1, its date and its reserved iteration number, and what that adds to DESIGN 11.1's memory carry-over asymmetry. Deliberately holds nothing about what was seen or written during it: recording that would make it an input to iteration 1 that no agent arm receives.

Korean comments documenting the rule-file schema: one rule per layer with patterns that match nothing (ZZZNEVERMATCHZZZ) and no corpus coupling. TEMPORARY — this file is deleted when the practice session ends, because iteration 1 must start from zero rules, and this entry is deleted with it. The stale-entry test is what enforces that: leaving the entry behind after deleting the file turns the suite red, which is the intended coupling rather than a nuisance.
The NOTE constant is a synthetic MIMIC-shaped header, invented for the test that proves the sniffer catches one. It comes from no corpus, which is why it can be committed.
This is the file that searches for that header, and its own docstring and CLINICAL_HEADER pattern quote it. Self-match, present since the first version.

The Korean is the note this tool writes: render() composes docs/notes/prompt-format-probe.md's headings, its rate and shape tables and the caption warning that a pooled fenced-versus-clean table can make a between-role difference look like a within-role correlate. Same false positive as tools/probe_call_variance.py's, one probe over — a tool whose output is Korean prose holds Korean prose as literals. It appeared only after the 2026-09-17 rate run added those tables; the earlier revision's Korean was under the sniffer's run threshold. It builds its prompts with the same assemble_* functions the arms use, sends a committed prompt template plus a filtered inventory and two label lists, and records outcome names, counts, token figures, wall seconds and hashes — no span, offset, matcher, prompt text or response text is printed, logged or written.

The corpus-comparison note. Its §7 and §9 are written in Korean, and §9 (added 2026-09-21) took the Hangul-run count over the sniffer's threshold of three — the file was under it before, so this is a new false positive rather than a newly noticed one. The Korean is this note's own analysis: section headings, the statement that a table is a table and not an interpretation, and the sentence recording that the measured direction disagrees with DESIGN §7. It cannot be note text, and not only because the sniffer's purpose is Korean note text: the two corpora this file compares are German and Spanish, so there is no Korean surface form in either corpus for it to have come from. No document id, no span index and no offset appears in the Korean, and nothing in this file is read out of sealed/.

Korean write-up of the en-deid port-oneshot run: cost, leak rate in both modes, the complementarity decomposition, the per-type table, the one rule that produced 98 of the 136 false positives, and the three-corpus comparison. Rule content is rule_id, layer and phi_type plus TWO PATTERNS QUOTED IN FULL — both are agent-authored regexes already committed in the rule file this note cites by path, and a regex is what the rule matches rather than what the corpus says. No span, offset, document id or note surface appears. The gold profiles are given as shapes with every digit replaced by 9 and every letter by A, and as token counts, precisely so that no date, place name or age surface is reproduced; the one AGE value stated (98) is the annotation threshold's consequence and is a count of years, not a person. The Korean is this note's own analysis, including the sentence recording that DESIGN 7's sharpest prediction is consistent with the aggregate while its mechanism is not where the leak came from.

acknowledged.why_real:
The first rule file written against the German layer of the mechanism vocabulary, and the first outside the es-meddocan series. 27 rule_ids, 8 findings, one unrecognised token each — no rule_id contributes two, so the finding count and the token count agree here. None of the eight is a person's name or a place name, which makes this a different population from the es-meddocan entries below and is the reason each was judged on 2026-09-21 rather than inherited. All eight are now REFUSED and this entry records violations and no pending work; no widening followed. Six were refused under step (1) of the expressibility test recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py — the token's mechanism sense is already sayable with accepted tokens, so refusing it takes nothing from the model. They are: a German preposition-article contraction in a date rule, which is the same refusal as the Spanish contraction on the iter5 entry and is sayable with the accepted preposition, article and particle tokens the German layer already holds; a German preposition of origin in a location rule, sayable with the accepted preposition that already means from; and four German compound nouns naming an identifier scheme's field label — a case number, a patient number, an insurance number and a file reference — each of which composes exactly from accepted tokens (case, patient, policy, record, number, id), with the German statutory-insurance abbreviation additionally already present in the code-token set. A seventh, the German word for colleague in a context-cue rule over the collegial letter frame, is refused on weaker ground and is recorded as such: the accepted role words doctor and arzt name the same mechanism approximately rather than exactly, so this is a near-synonym refusal of the kind the iter7 entry flagged as an honest edge, not a provably costless one. That caveat still stands and is not discharged by the eighth judgement.

The eighth was the one token left UNJUDGED when this entry was first written, and it was judged on 2026-09-21 and REFUSED. It is the two-letter abbreviation of the German word for doctor, in a prefix rule over the honorific. Two things had to be separated first, because this layer holds two abbreviation pairs on purpose (str beside strasse, plz beside postleitzahl) and together they look like a standing permission for 'the abbreviation of a word we already accept'. They are not one category: plz shortens the NAME OF A SCHEME and belongs with cp, nif and kvnr in the code-token set, while str is not a shortening at all but a DISTINCT SURFACE CUE, appearing compounded where the full form does not, so a rule matching one is not the rule matching the other and step (1) never applies. The doctor abbreviation is neither. It names no scheme — there is no ordering, digit count or check digit to describe, which is what separates it from iso — and the mechanism of its rule, an honorific marker preceding a name opening a NAME window, is sayable EXACTLY with accepted tokens: doktor in this layer, prefix, title and abbrev in the English vocabulary, composing to doktor_abbrev_prefix_name if the author wants the abbreviation recorded in the name. So step (1) refuses it at zero cost, and this is the same refusal as iter8's abbreviation of 'international' rather than a conflict with it: opening 'abbreviation of a word we already hold in full' is the strictly worse vocabulary that entry named. gaz is not a counter-case, because gazetteer is a mechanism word and a naming.yaml layer axis value, so gaz shortens the name of a mechanism category while doktor is a language-layer commonplace. It is worth recording what this refusal is NOT: the token cannot point at an individual, and it is exactly the honorific category the exclusion notes admit when they say a title is a marker that precedes a name and not the name. The judgement order puts expressibility before category membership, so it ended at step (1) and never reached that question. The reasoning is recorded in release_screen.py beside the judgement order, not only here, because the next German arm writing the same token is repeating this judgement rather than raising a new one.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, and the reason is not a frozen prompt. This is a single-call arm: there is no round 2 to write a better name in, so the file is final the moment it is scored and nothing in the arm can repair it. The pin stays at EIGHT, because the token that could have moved it was refused rather than admitted — the count was written to break in exactly one way, by judging the doctor abbreviation, and judging it as a refusal is the branch that leaves the count standing and turns this entry into a clean set of refusals. The near-synonym caveat on the colleague token is the only soft edge left, and it is recorded above rather than resolved: refusing a near-synonym has low cost, not provably zero. The count does not break again from this file's side. It would only move if an accepted token were re-judged, and the record forbids that — re-judging accepted tokens is a backward widening that breaks counts fixed across arms. Note also what did not happen: the abbreviation question was raised on the German layer's own pairs rather than on this file, as the earlier wording required, and the answer was that those pairs are two different things and neither licenses a third.

acknowledged.why_real: Two rule_ids in this arm's round-4 rule file name a rule by its content rather than by its mechanism: each embeds a place name as the identifier of a gazetteer or pattern rule. That is Prohibition 2 of docs/prompts/rule_author.md, and the mechanism-vocabulary check caught it correctly. The tokens were judged on 2026-08-24 during the sixth widening and REFUSED — admitting place names would turn the vocabulary into 'everything that is not a person's name' and weaken the surname-ingress check that is the whole point of it. So this is not a widening that has not happened yet; it is a violation with no legitimate repair.
acknowledged.fixed_when: It is not fixed in this arm. docs/prompts/rule_author.md is frozen for the duration of the port-loop arm (DESIGN §6.3), so the prompt that produced the name cannot be strengthened without making every round of this arm a different arm. The entry clears when the arm's rule files are superseded or when a future arm runs against a prompt that states the mechanism/content distinction, whichever comes first. The pinned sniff count is what keeps it honest: a widening that reduced the finding count would break the pin and force this entry to be re-argued rather than silently inherited.

acknowledged.why_real: Round 5's rule file repeats round 4's two content-named place tokens — same violation, same refusal, and worth noting as a recurrence rather than a new fact, because the frozen prompt gives the model no way to learn from round 4's finding. It also carries four further tokens the vocabulary does not have: one Spanish age-band word, one Spanish clinical formula word, and two that read as genuine mechanism words (a prefix mechanism and a punctuation-delimiter mechanism). Three of those four — the age-band word, the clinical formula word and the prefix mechanism — were judged on 2026-08-24 with round 6's tokens and REFUSED, each because its mechanism sense is already sayable with accepted tokens (see the expressibility test recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py). So this entry now covers five refusals and one genuinely unjudged token: the punctuation-delimiter mechanism, which appears in round 5's file and not in round 6's and was therefore outside that judgement's scope.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, for the frozen-prompt reason on the iter4 entry. The pinned count stays six because the 2026-08-24 judgement refused every token it looked at and widened nothing — a refusal changes what this entry says, not what the screener finds. What can still move it is the one unjudged token: the punctuation-delimiter mechanism is the strongest remaining candidate for a seventh widening, since no accepted token names a specific mark while slash/dash/dot/colon show the project treats which-mark as mechanism, and it cannot designate anyone so admitting it costs nothing. Judging it will drop this count to five and break the pin, which is the intended coupling.

acknowledged.why_real: All eight findings were judged on 2026-08-24 and all eight are REFUSED, so this entry records violations and no pending work. Two are the content-named place tokens rounds 4 and 5 also carry, for the reason on the iter4 entry. The other six were each refused under the expressibility test now recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py: a token whose mechanism sense is already sayable with accepted tokens is refused, because refusing it takes nothing from the model — the literal word it names belongs in the rule's terms or cue, which is where Prohibition 2 puts content. They are a Spanish range preposition (sayable as range plus years), the Spanish clinical episode word (its English form is already in the vocabulary), a single-letter prefix mechanism (sayable as prefix), a structural word for the introductory position of an age mention (sayable as header, context or before), a Spanish age-band word (its own rule_id already carries age and infant), and a Spanish street-type word that is also the name of an Andalusian town. Round 6 dropped iter5's punctuation-delimiter token, so the count moving six to eight is not six-plus-two.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, for the frozen-prompt reason on the iter4 entry, and there is no widening pending on these eight — the pin at eight is stable until the arm's rule files are superseded, because a judgement that refuses everything changes what this entry says and not what the screener finds. The street-type-or-town token is the case worth reading before the next such judgement: it is the first time the street-type versus street-name distinction was not formal, and the reasoning is kept beside the exclusion categories rather than here because the next arm will meet the shape and not this path.

acknowledged.why_real: All thirteen findings were judged on 2026-08-25 and all thirteen are REFUSED, so this entry records violations and no pending work. Thirteen findings carry fifteen unrecognised tokens, which is new: this is the first rule file in the arm where a single rule_id contributed two of them, so the finding count and the token count diverge and neither is a typo for the other. Eight of the fifteen are round 6's, refused there and unchanged here. The seven new ones were each refused under the expressibility test recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py — step (1), which asks whether the token's mechanism sense is already sayable with accepted tokens and refuses it if so, because then refusing takes nothing from the model. They are: a further country name, in a regex rule over that country's city and region names, which is the third place name in the arm and the same refusal as rounds 4 to 6 rather than a new question; the Spanish word for 'other', whose English form the vocabulary already holds as a phi_type axis value; an English age-band word, refused because the age-band category the sixth widening created is already filled with three tokens covering that band; a Spanish preposition-article contraction and the Spanish word for month, both from one age rule whose mechanism is an age written in months and is sayable as age plus months, with the contraction itself covered by the accepted preposition, article and particle tokens; and two English industry words from a gazetteer rule whose phi_type is ORGANISATION and whose terms are three company names — the rule works by list membership over company names, and which industry those companies are in is a property of the terms, which is where Prohibition 2 puts content. Two of the seven are worth naming as the honest edges of this judgement. The age-band refusal is the first in the arm to rest on near-synonyms rather than on an exact accepted equivalent: the refused word is the plainest English name for that band and the sixth widening's list omitted it while admitting three Latinate neighbours, so the cost of refusal is low rather than provably zero. And the 'other' refusal is discharged by a token that entered the vocabulary as a naming.yaml axis value and not as a mechanism word, which means step (1)'s supply of accepted tokens is wider than the mechanism argument that justifies it.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, for the frozen-prompt reason on the iter4 entry, and there is no widening pending on these thirteen — the pin at thirteen is stable until the arm's rule files are superseded, because a judgement that refuses everything changes what this entry says and not what the screener finds. Round 7 is the round that made the ceiling ending certain, not the arm's last round — the ceiling is 8, so one more rule file follows this one, and the sentence that first stood here said otherwise and was wrong. The count rising 8 to 13 across one round is itself the finding to carry forward: the frozen prompt does not converge on mechanism naming, it accumulates content names at roughly the rate it adds rules. The two edges named above belong in the next arm's vocabulary design rather than in a seventh widening here — the age-band gap because filling a category by instance is what left it, and the axis-value question because it decides whether step (1) may be discharged by tokens admitted for reasons other than mechanism.

acknowledged.why_real: All eleven findings were judged on 2026-08-25 and all eleven are REFUSED, so this entry records violations and no pending work. Eleven findings carry thirteen unrecognised tokens: two rule_ids each contribute two, so the divergence round 7 first showed persists and neither number is a typo for the other. Twelve of the thirteen are inherited and were refused in rounds 4 to 7 — the count fell because round 8 removed fifteen rules and three of the round-7 tokens left with them (the Spanish country name, the street-type word that is also an Andalusian town, and the Spanish word for 'other'), not because any earlier refusal was revisited. Exactly one token is new: an English abbreviation of 'international', in a regex rule over the international dialling prefix of a phone number. It is refused under step (1) of the expressibility test recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py, and it is the cleanest refusal in the arm — the mechanism is sayable exactly rather than approximately, because country, code, prefix, phone and number are all already accepted and compose into the same name. It is also worth recording why it has no home even as an abbreviation: RULE_ID_ALLOWED_TOKENS exists for national identifier-scheme abbreviations and its entire content is such schemes, so admitting a contraction of an ordinary English word there would open 'abbreviation of a word we already accept in full' as a category, which is a strictly worse vocabulary than the one that already holds the full word.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, for the frozen-prompt reason on the iter4 entry. This is the arm's last rule file — round 8 is the pre-registered ceiling and the arm terminated there (DESIGN §3) — so this is the last entry of the series, and the pin at eleven is stable until the arm's rule files are superseded. The finding worth carrying forward is what the fall from thirteen to eleven does and does not show. It is the same fact as the rule file shrinking 66 to 60: the pruning removed content-named rules along with the rest, so the count tracks how many such rules survive and not whether the model learned to name by mechanism. Against that, one new content-shaped token still entered in the round that removed fifteen rules, and the twelve survivors are unchanged. Read across rounds 4 to 8 the series is 2, 6, 8, 13, 11 — the frozen prompt neither converges nor monotonically degrades; it produces content names at a rate set by how many rules it is writing.

acknowledged.why_real: The first rule file written against the English layer of the mechanism vocabulary, and the first for a corpus whose language layer is EMPTY — RULE_ID_VOCAB_BY_LANG['en'] has no entries, because the 230-token mechanism vocabulary is itself English, so there is no 'clinical formula in that language' tier to fall back on here. 30 rule_ids, 13 findings, 19 token instances and 17 distinct tokens: four rule_ids contribute two or three each, so the finding count and the token count diverge further than in any earlier file and neither is a typo for the other. ALL 17 ARE REFUSED and this entry records violations and no pending work; no widening followed, and the pin stays at 13. Three refusals are not new judgements. 'us', from a phone-format rule and a postal-code rule, is a country name, and country and place names were refused categorically on 2026-08-24 (the espana entries below) on the ground that admitting them turns the vocabulary into 'everything that is not a person's name' and weakens the surname-ingress check; that refusal does its work at the category and does not need the expressibility test. 'intl' is the SAME TOKEN, in the same mechanism — the international dialling prefix of a phone number — that iter8 refused on 2026-08-25, and the composition named there (country, code, prefix, phone, number) applies unchanged. 'dr' repeats the German layer's eighth judgement of 2026-09-21 a fortiori: that judgement refused the German doctor abbreviation by composing doctor_abbrev_prefix_name out of the ENGLISH vocabulary, which is the layer this file is in. The other fourteen were judged on 2026-09-21 under step (1) of the expressibility test recorded beside the exclusion categories in release_screen.py — a token whose mechanism sense is already sayable with accepted tokens is refused, because refusing it takes nothing from the model. 'mr', 'mrs', 'ms' and 'prof' are honorific abbreviations whose mechanism is a title preceding a name opening a NAME window, said exactly by title_prefix_name; WHICH titles is content and is already in the rule's own cue list. 'md' is the same marker after the name: title_suffix_name. 'old', which appears in two rule_ids, is the cleanest refusal in the file — it is a literal alternative inside the rule's own regex, and the mechanism is an age written as a number plus a unit, said exactly by age_years_pattern and age_months_pattern. 'po' and 'box' are the two words of a postal-delivery address form, said by postal_address_pattern, and again both words are in the pattern. 'apt' and 'suite' are sub-unit markers inside an address and unit, address and label are all accepted: address_unit_label. 'employed' and 'as' are the two words of a context cue introducing an occupation, said by occupation_cue or profession_context_cue, with the cue words belonging in cue. Two of the fourteen are worth naming as this judgement's honest edges, in the same spirit as the German colleague token below. 'zip' is the only token in the file with a real counter-argument: RULE_ID_ALLOWED_TOKENS exists for identifier-scheme abbreviations and it already holds cp, which is the Spanish postal code — so the parallel 'ZIP is the name of the US postal-code scheme' is not frivolous. It fails for a reason specific to the layer: cp is in that set because a Spanish rule file names the scheme in Spanish and no accepted Spanish word for postal code exists, whereas postal and code are BOTH accepted here, so postal_code_pattern says the mechanism exactly and the five-plus-four digit shape the regex encodes is not a property of which country uses it. Recording the counter-argument matters more than the outcome: the next English arm writing zip is repeating this judgement rather than raising a new one. 'state' is a near-synonym refusal — region and area are accepted and city_region_pattern says the mechanism, but a state is a particular kind of region rather than the same thing, so the cost of refusing is low rather than provably zero. That is the same weaker ground the German colleague token is on, and it is the second such edge in as many new-corpus arms.
acknowledged.fixed_when: Not in this arm, and the reason is not a frozen prompt. This is a single-call arm: there is no round 2 to write a better name in, so the file is final the moment it is scored and nothing in the arm can repair it. The pin stays at THIRTEEN and it is a finding count, not a token count — 19 instances over 17 distinct tokens, with four rule_ids contributing more than one. It moves only if a token is re-judged, and the record forbids re-judging accepted tokens because that is a backward widening that breaks counts fixed across arms. What the next English arm should carry forward is the layer fact rather than any single token: an EMPTY RULE_ID_VOCAB_BY_LANG['en'] means every English surface word a rule matches has nowhere to go except the pattern or the cue, which is exactly where Prohibition 2 puts it — so the English layer is the one layer where step (1) should refuse nearly everything, and this file's 17-for-17 is the predicted shape rather than a surprise. The two edges recorded above (zip against cp, state against region) belong in the next arm's vocabulary design, not in a widening here.
